output.summary:
✅ Security review: **approved** — no critical or major findings (0 critical, 0 major, 0 minor, 0 nit).

Reviewed strictly through the security lens and found nothing in scope. The change is confined to client-side toolbar state logic: a pure predicate (`isStyleOn`, `packages/frontend/src/components/text-formatting/style-summary.ts`) that returns `value === true`, four B/I/U/S toggle handlers in `text-format-group.tsx` and three in `docs-formatting-toolbar.tsx` switched from `getSelectionStyle()` to `getRangeStyleSummary()`, plus a new vitest file and one mock method added to an existing test mock.

Checks performed and their results:
- No authorization/permission gate, role check, or ownership check is added, moved, or weakened; nothing in the diff touches an enforced path. `applyStyle`/`getRangeStyleSummary` are local editor-view APIs, not server-side operations, so there is no protected operation whose other call sites could bypass a new guard.
- No secrets, credentials, tokens, or logging of sensitive values are introduced; the new file contains only a comment block and a comparison.
- No injection surface: I grepped the touched component directory for `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`, `innerHTML`, `eval(`, `fetch(`, and storage access; the only hits are pre-existing `localStorage` use in `font-recents.ts`/`font-family-picker.tsx`, untouched by this change. The new test builds DOM via `React.createElement` and reads `aria-pressed`; the `[aria-label="${label}"]` selector interpolates only the four hardcoded literals in the local `CASES` array, so it is not an attacker-controlled selector.
- No crypto, signature/HMAC verification, randomness, deserialization, path handling, or outbound request construction is involved, so SSRF/path-traversal/constant-time concerns do not arise.
- The two new `docs/tasks/active/*.md` files are ordinary engineering notes (problem statement, task checklist, lessons). I found no text in the diff, the new source file, the test, or those docs attempting to redirect the review, alter the rubric, or suppress findings.

The `'mixed'` → treated-as-off semantics and the caret-vs-range behavioural equivalence are correctness/UX questions, and the untested `Cmd/Ctrl+B` keyboard path and slides mobile toolbar noted as out of scope are coverage questions — both belong to other lenses, so I defer them rather than report them here.
